title: Is There Shareholder Expropriation in the United States? An Analysis of Publicly Traded Subsidiaries

rival_explanations: market timing hypothesis (parents divest ahead of anticipated underperformance rather than expropriate via operational transactions)
reduced monitoring effort by the parent as its stake falls (not expropriation)
negative market reaction driven by the seasoned equity offering used to execute the change, not expropriation

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (publicly traded U.S. subsidiaries created via equity carveouts; peers matched within Fama-French 48-industry portfolios)

analyses.label: [withheld: wording matches the source]
analyses.sample: 264 equity carveouts, Years 0-4 following carveout; t-test of means and rank test of medians for parent vs. subsidiary ROA

key_ivs.name: parent ownership category
key_ivs.measure: 3 groups by fraction of shares owned by parent at end of year: Fully Divested (<5%), Ownership Below 50% (5%-50%), Ownership Above 50% (>50%)

analyses.label: Table 3 - Peer-Adjusted Operating ROA of Subsidiaries by Ownership Level

key_ivs.measure: Fully Divested (<5%), Ownership Below 50% (5%-50%), Ownership Above 50% (>50%)

dv.name: subsidiary peer-adjusted operating ROA (Years 1-4)
dv.measure: peer-adjusted operating ROA (operating cash flow, Compustat item 13 / total assets, item 6; matched to Fama-French 48-industry Year-0 peers), winsorized 1st/99th
